introduction: Today we begin Holy Week. We welcome Jesus into Jerusalem as the crowd cries, Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord. Then we hear the Passion according to Saint Luke, in which Jesus forgives those who crucify him and promises Paradise to a dying thief. Paul sings of Christ who emptied himself and became obedient to death. Let us follow Jesus this week to the cross and the empty tomb.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, Christ humbled himself for us, even to death on a cross. Let us pray to the Father, who exalted him.
intentions: For the Church as she enters Holy Week: that she may follow Christ with faith and love. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peace in Jerusalem and in all places of conflict: that the King who comes in peace may reign in every heart. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are condemned unjustly, mocked or tortured: that they may find strength in Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the dying, especially those who die without hope: that they may hear Christ say, today you will be with me in Paradise. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may forgive those who hurt us, as Jesus forgave from the cross. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Almighty Father, your Son entered Jerusalem to give his life for us. Help us to follow him faithfully this week, and to rise with him at Easter. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Remember me
reflection.body:
Luke tells the entry into Jerusalem with joy. As Jesus rides down the Mount of Olives, "the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice." They cry, "Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!" When some ask Jesus to silence them, he answers, "if these were silent, the stones would cry out."

Luke's account of the Passion shows the mercy of Jesus at every step. At the Last Supper, he gives his Body and Blood: "This is my body which is given for you. Do this in memory of me." He tells Peter that he has prayed for him, "that your faith wouldn't fail." In the garden, when one of his followers cuts off a servant's ear, Jesus touches the ear and heals him.

After Peter denies him three times, "The Lord turned and looked at Peter." That look of love breaks Peter's heart, and "He went out, and wept bitterly."

On the way to the cross, Jesus comforts the women of Jerusalem. On the cross, he prays for those who crucify him: "Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing." One of the criminals crucified with him asks, "Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom." Jesus answers, "Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise." His last words are a prayer of trust: "Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!"

Paul's hymn sums it up: Christ "humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, yes, the death of the cross. Therefore God also highly exalted him."

This week, take time for the liturgies of the Triduum if you can. And pray the thief's prayer often: Jesus, remember me.
